name: Jaldapara Tourist Lodge (WBTDC)
summary: The West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation lodge at Madarihat, right by the entry to Jaldapara National Park. Plain, spacious and well placed for early safaris.
body: This is the large government lodge on the main road at Madarihat, a short walk from Madarihat station and a few minutes from the park gate. Rooms are simple and clean rather than stylish, with a garden, a dining hall serving Bengali and North Indian food, and a small wildlife museum in the compound.

Its real value is location. Safari jeeps leave from close by, and the staff are used to guests who need breakfast packed for a 6 am start. Since the fire that destroyed the old Hollong lodge inside the park in June 2024, this is the best-known government place to stay for Jaldapara.
why: A short drive to the park gate and safari counter
Government-run, with fair, published tariffs
Big enough to have rooms when smaller places are full
Walking distance of Madarihat railway station

faqs.q: Can the Jaldapara Tourist Lodge book my safari?
faqs.a: The lodge staff help guests with the Jaldapara jeep safari and point you to the right counter, but slots are controlled by the forest department and released online and at the Madarihat counter. Book online when possible and treat the lodge as a back-up for remaining slots. Rules have changed several times in recent seasons. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I book the Jaldapara Tourist Lodge?
faqs.a: Book through the West Bengal Tourism Development Corporation's official booking system or its Kolkata and Siliguri offices. Avoid unofficial sites that add large mark-ups. Rooms for the Durga Puja holidays, Christmas and New Year sell out weeks ahead, so book a month or more in advance for those dates.

faqs.q: Is food available at the lodge?
faqs.a: Yes. The lodge has a dining hall serving simple Bengali and North Indian meals, with fish, chicken and vegetarian options. Order dinner in the afternoon, as the kitchen cooks to numbers. Ask for a packed breakfast or early tea if you have a dawn safari; there is little else open in Madarihat before 6 am.

name: Murti (Banani) Eco-Tourism Centre, WBFDC
summary: The West Bengal Forest Development Corporation lodge beside the Murti river near Gorumara, with a main building, cottages and tents in a large garden. Guests can arrange Gorumara safaris at reception.
body: Banani sits on the bank of the Murti river, about 15 km from Lataguri, with the edge of Gorumara forest across the water. You can walk down to the stony riverbed in the evening and listen to peafowl and barking deer from the far bank. Rooms range from tents and standard rooms to deluxe and premium categories.

Because it is run by the forest corporation, the reception can usually book Gorumara and Chapramari safari and watchtower slots for guests, which saves queueing at the public counter in Lataguri. Meals are simple and served at fixed times.
why: Riverside setting on the Murti
Safari bookings at reception for guests
A wide range of room prices, from tents upwards
Quieter than the lodges on the Lataguri highway

faqs.q: How far is Murti Banani from Gorumara safari gates?
faqs.a: It is about 15 km from Lataguri, where the main Gorumara counter is, a drive of around 30 minutes. Some safari routes leave from points closer to Murti. Ask reception which gate your slot uses and leave early for dawn slots, as wild elephants sometimes block the road around sunrise.

faqs.q: How do I book Murti Banani?
faqs.a: Book on the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation website at wbfdc.net, where the Jalpaiguri properties are listed with room types and tariffs. Prices shown there were about ₹1,500 for a tent and ₹1,800–4,000 for rooms when we last checked, before taxes. Tariffs are indicative and change each season.

faqs.q: Is it safe to walk by the Murti river at night?
faqs.a: No. Stay inside the lodge compound after dark. Elephants, gaur and occasionally leopards move along the river and forest edge at night. Evening walks on the riverbed are fine before sunset, close to the lodge and with others. Follow the staff's advice, especially in the early and late season.

name: Sinclairs Retreat Dooars
summary: A large hilltop resort at Chalsa, about 15 km from Lataguri, with cottage-style rooms, a pool and views over the Dooars plains. The most comfortable base for Gorumara and Samsing.
body: Sinclairs sits on the Chalsa hilltop in about 20 acres of garden, looking down over tea estates and the Gorumara forest towards the plains. Rooms are in cottage blocks with private balconies, and there is a swimming pool, a children's pool, a multicuisine restaurant and a bar.

It is a good choice for families and couples who want comfort between safaris. From here Gorumara, Murti, Samsing and Jhalong are all within an hour, and the staff can arrange cars and help with safari bookings. It is busy with Kolkata families during the Puja and winter holidays.
why: The most comfortable large resort in the western Dooars
Pool and big grounds for children
Central for Gorumara, Murti and Samsing
Reliable service and food

faqs.q: How far is Sinclairs Retreat Dooars from Gorumara?
faqs.a: The resort is on the Chalsa hilltop, about 15 km and 25–30 minutes from Lataguri and the main Gorumara safari counter. Murti is about 10 km away and Samsing about 20 km. For a dawn safari you will leave the resort around 5 am, so arrange a packed breakfast the night before.

The front desk can help with safari bookings and cars, but slots are controlled by the forest department and sold online and at the Lataguri counter. Ask the resort to confirm your slot before you arrive in peak season. Safari fees are paid separately from the room. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Sinclairs Retreat Dooars good for children?
faqs.a: Yes. It has a children's pool, open lawns, bicycles and a restaurant that can cook simple food. Rooms are spread over a slope, so ask for a block near the main building if you have small children or older relatives. Book early for school holidays.

name: Mendabari Jungle Lodge, WBFDC
summary: A small forest corporation lodge inside the Chilapata and Mendabari forest near Jaldapara. Simple rooms, real forest at the door and very few people.
body: Mendabari Jungle Lodge is run by the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation in the forest between Jaldapara and Chilapata. It is a quiet place with a handful of rooms, a watch point over the forest and almost no traffic at night apart from the sounds of the jungle.

This is not a resort. Power can fail, food is home-style and fixed, and mobile signal is patchy. In return you get a real night in the forest, with easy access to Chilapata safaris and the Jaldapara gates. Book early because there are very few rooms.
why: A true forest stay with very few rooms
Close to both Chilapata and Jaldapara
Run by the forest corporation, with fair rates
Good birding at dawn

faqs.q: How do I book Mendabari Jungle Lodge?
faqs.a: Book on the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation website at wbfdc.net under the Alipurduar properties. When we last checked, super deluxe rooms were listed at about ₹2,500 a night before taxes. Rooms are few, so book four to six weeks ahead for the winter season. Tariffs are indicative.

It suits children who enjoy nature and early nights. There is no pool, no television and little to do after dark except listen to the forest. Keep children inside the compound after sunset, as elephants and other animals pass close by. For a more relaxed family stay, use Mendabari for one night only.

faqs.q: Can I do the Chilapata safari from Mendabari?
faqs.a: Yes. The Chilapata jeep safari, which usually visits the Nal Raja Garh ruins, starts from the Kodalbasti side of the forest, a short drive from the lodge. The lodge can help you arrange a jeep and guide. Safaris stop from 16 June to 15 September. Check current status before you travel.

name: Suntalekhola Eco Tourism Centre, WBFDC
summary: Forest corporation cottages and tents beside the Suntalekhola stream above Samsing, reached over a hanging footbridge. Cheap, green and quiet.
body: The Suntalekhola lodge sits in forest a few kilometres above Samsing, where the Suntalekhola stream comes down to meet the Murti. You cross a small suspension bridge to reach the cottages, which stand among tall trees with the sound of water all day. Tents are the cheapest option; deluxe and super deluxe rooms cost a little more.

It makes a calm base for walks to Rocky Island, Samsing's tea gardens and the edge of Neora Valley National Park. Food is simple and comes from the lodge kitchen. Nights are cool, around 10–15°C in winter, so bring a fleece.
why: One of the cheapest forest stays in the Dooars
Stream-side cottages in real forest
A short walk to Samsing tea gardens
Run by the forest corporation

faqs.q: How do I get to Suntalekhola from Siliguri?
faqs.a: Drive about 90 km via Sevoke, Malbazar, Chalsa and Matelli to Samsing, then a few more kilometres up to Suntalekhola, about 3 hours in all. A reserved car costs roughly ₹3,000–4,000. On a budget, take a bus to Chalsa or Malbazar and a shared jeep to Samsing, then a local car for the last stretch.

Book on the West Bengal Forest Development Corporation website at wbfdc.net, where it is listed under the Kalimpong properties as Suntalekhola Eco Tourism Centre. Tents were listed at about ₹1,500 and rooms at ₹2,500–3,000 when we last checked, before taxes. Prices are indicative.

faqs.q: Is Suntalekhola open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Suntalekhola is outside the national parks, so it is not covered by the 16 June to 15 September park closure, but heavy rain can damage the road and swell the stream. The forest corporation sometimes closes cottages for repairs. Check current status before you travel.

name: Santalabari, Buxa and Lepchakha homestays
price_band: ₹1,200–2,000 per person per night with meals
summary: Simple family homestays in the villages on the walk to Buxa Fort, run mostly by Drukpa and Nepali-speaking families. Basic rooms, home food and forest all round.
body: Several families in Santalabari at the start of the Buxa Fort path, and in Buxa village and Lepchakha above it, offer rooms to walkers. Expect a clean bed, shared or simple attached bathrooms, solar or erratic power, and three home-cooked meals of rice, dal, vegetables and sometimes chicken or eggs.

These villages lie inside Buxa Tiger Reserve, and rules on homestays here have tightened in recent years, with some closed after court and forest department orders. Ask the guide counter at Santalabari or your Alipurduar driver which homestays are currently allowed. Check current status before you travel.
why: Sleep up by the fort and see Lepchakha at sunrise
Money goes straight to village families
Home food and local guides
The cheapest way to stay in Buxa

faqs.q: Do I need to book Buxa homestays in advance?
faqs.a: In the winter season and on long weekends, yes. Phone ahead through your driver, a local contact or the trek guide counter at Santalabari. Outside peak dates you can often find a room on arrival, but which homestays are allowed to operate changes with forest rules. Check current status before you travel.

Expect roughly ₹1,200–2,000 per person per night, including dinner, breakfast and often lunch. Porters to carry bags up from Santalabari cost extra, and the local guide fee is paid separately. Prices are indicative and rise at peak times. Carry cash, as there are no ATMs or card machines in the villages.

faqs.q: Is there electricity and mobile signal at Buxa?
faqs.a: Power is limited and often solar, so charge devices when you can and carry a power bank and torch. Mobile signal is patchy around the fort and Lepchakha; one or two networks work at points along the path. Tell someone your plans before you walk up.
